##### Random network NPSEM and graph generators

A random network NPSEM (RNNPSEM, @def-npsem-ne) has two kinds of equation. *Structural* equations represent constructs measured on each observational unit; *relational* equations represent the causal processes linking constructs across observational units. A graph generator is the matrix of relational variables, one for each ordered pair of distinct nodes, giving the entries of a random network graph. The network is directed: $\psi_t(i,j)$ is the weight of $j$'s influence on $i$, and need not equal $\psi_t(j,i)$. In a general random network, single-world independence takes each graph generator as a single variable: the network must be independent of the structural counterfactuals, and nothing is assumed about how edges within a generator depend on each other. In a bipartite random network (@def-bipartite-npsem-ie), a tie between a person and a place runs both ways with the same weight, so the people's rows determine the network. Each person's row of the adjacency matrix, their network weights, is one variable in their observational unit, so the network becomes person-level data and single-world independence holds row by row: a person's links to different places may share a disturbance.
